description: Three rows of eight steps sharing one probability per step: each clock advances a step, a random draw against that probability sets whether it plays, and all three rows put out a voltage

params.text: Sets the internal clock, 15 to 960 bpm, which drives the sequence whenever the clock jack is empty
Sets the voltage this step puts on the 1 output when the step plays, -10V to 10V
Sets the voltage this step puts on the 2 output when the step plays, -10V to 10V
Sets the voltage this step puts on the 3 output when the step plays, -10V to 10V
Sets the chance that this step plays, 0 to 100 per cent, and it applies to all three rows at once; a cable in the jack below replaces the knob entirely
Chooses which row reaches the out jack: below 1 the first row, from 1 up to below 2 the second, at 2 the third

inputs.text: A rising edge advances the sequence by one step, and the level has to reach 2V for a single step; with nothing patched the internal clock is used instead
Replaces the probability knob above it for that step, 0V to 1V, with anything outside that range clamped into it
Replaces the track knob, 0V to 2V: below 1V the first row reaches the out jack, 1V up to below 2V the second, exactly 2V the third
Any voltage above 0V restarts the sequence, so that the next clock plays the first step

outputs.text: 10V while its own step is the current one and that step played, and 0V at all other times
10V for about a hundred samples each time a step plays, whatever the row and whatever the step
The first row's voltage from the last step that played, held until another step plays
The second row's voltage from the last step that played, held until another step plays
The third row's voltage from the last step that played, held until another step plays
The voltage of whichever row the track control selects, taken from the last step that played

notes: The internal clock runs from the moment the module is placed, so the sequence advances with nothing patched at all.
An external clock must reach 2V. Between 1V and 2V the module advances a step on every sample, because it subtracts one volt from the value it compares against.
A step that does not play leaves all four voltage outputs holding what the last step that played put there, and turns that step's indicator red rather than green.
The trigger output is about a hundred samples long however the module is clocked, so it shortens in time as the sample rate rises.
The module has no menu of its own beyond Rack's.
